title: Ordinary coefficient extension on the profinite slice
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring, S a profinite set, and phi the direct scalar map from the constant sheaf Lambda(*) on the slice to the reconstructed section-ring sheaf of the restricted Lambda. For any two cochain extension models along the point scalar map and phi, their ordinary functors satisfy a natural isomorphism: extend coefficients, pass from section modules to internal modules, and apply actual slice mapMod; or restrict the original modules by commutativeConstantSliceRestriction, extend along phi, and pass to slice internal modules. The maps phi, the equivalences, and restriction are those of def-zl-condensed-lisse-evaluation-model and lem-zl-commutative-constant-slice-restriction. No complexes or derived functors occur in the conclusion.

source.place: Equations (3.1)-(3.2), Remark 3.2; Stacks Modules on Sites, Tags 03CY, 03DH and 03EK

proof.text: Reconstruct the canonical isomorphism of ring sheaves from the monoidal comparison between restriction of underlying presheaves and the underlying presheaf of slice restriction. Its components are identities on additive groups. Comparing the lax tensor maps identifies restriction of sectionwise modules with actual internal-module mapMod after the sectionModuleEquivalence.

Apply the constant-sheaf adjunction to the restricted scalar map. Precomposing with the constant-presheaf sheafification unit reduces the equality to naturality along the map from a slice object to its terminal object. The terminal component is profiniteSectionRingIso, so this is precisely the stated direct scalar map phi.

Extension of scalars is left adjoint to scalar restriction, by the existing ordinary coefficient adjunction and the object and map equations of each model. Slice restriction, with coefficient isomorphism transport, is left adjoint to pushforward along Over.star. The scalar square identifies the two composite right adjoints, using the composition formula for module pushforward. Uniqueness of left adjoints yields the ordinary extension/restriction comparison. Conjugate by the section-module equivalences to obtain the displayed natural isomorphism. This argument does not require nonempty objects or nonzero rings.

theorem profinite_coefficient_slice_ordinary
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X] (S : Profinite.{u})
    (φ : realizationRing ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S)
        (condensedScalarRing Λ.X) ⟶
      Evaluation.ringSheaf ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S)
        (profiniteCoefficient Λ.X S))
    (hφ : φ =
      (constantSheaf ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (profiniteScalarMap Λ.X S)) ≫
        Evaluation.scalarMap ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S)
          (profiniteCoefficient Λ.X S) (Over.mk (𝟙 S)) Over.mkIdTerminal)
    (M : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 2, u + 2}
      (condensedScalarMap Λ.X))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2}
      (realizationModules ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S)
        (condensedScalarRing Λ.X))]
    (MS : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 2, u + 2} φ) :
    let e := InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionModuleEquivalence
      (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Λ.X
    let eS := InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionModuleEquivalence
      ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over S) (profiniteCoefficient Λ.X S)
    let f := ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).overPullback Ab.{u + 1} S).mapMod Λ.X
    Nonempty (M.E ⋙ e.inverse ⋙ f ≅
      commutativeConstantSliceRestriction (coherentTopology Profinite.{u})
        (condensedScalarRing Λ.X) S ⋙ MS.E ⋙ eS.inverse)
